correctness.rationale: For every N>=2 and 0<q<1, normalized Bergman kernels give G_ab=(1-q)^2/(1-q omega^(a-b))^2. Cyclic DFT isolates n congruent to j and sums (n+1)q^n, giving the exact spectrum. Consecutive ratios strictly decrease in j. T_N(e^-h) has derivative -1/(4sinh(h/2)^2)+N^2/(4sinh(Nh/2)^2)<0 since sinh(Nu)>N sinh u. Strict log concavity and f(q)=1+(N-1)q^N-Nq^(N-1)>0 certify the least mode. Uniform in 0<=j<N expansions of q_N^j and q_N^N give O_c(N^-1), then F_c has its unique maximum x_c and equal endpoint minima. The checker separately computes Gram DFTs and finite limiting profiles in 177 cases. Scientific risks: computations are samples; the proof is written for fixed c, not c depending on N.

value.rationale: Sharp Riesz bounds for normalized point evaluations measure the stability of finite Hilbert-space interpolation. For each finite N and every radius, the theorem determines the best/worst Fourier modes and ALL mode transition radii without enumeration; it uncovers interior norming modes absent in analogous Szego kernels. The full critical radial N-scaled spectrum, limiting mode fraction x_c and elementary explicit condition number quantify when finite regular-polygon interpolation remains stable. A complete exact parametric classification is intrinsically useful and not an arbitrary numerical invariant; no downstream major theorem is claimed.
